pros: Pricing tables with optional line items calculate totals before signing
Documents generate from HubSpot, Salesforce or Pipedrive records with fields prefilled
Content library and locked blocks keep legal wording consistent across reps
Recipients can comment in context and pay by card at signature
Page level analytics show where each recipient spent time
cons: Overkill and costly if you only need a signature on a PDF
Web editor does not round trip with Word tracked changes
SSO, bulk send and higher API limits sit on top tier or add ons
starting_price: $19 per user per month billed annually
verdict_line: Pick PandaDoc if your team builds, prices and signs proposals or quotes from a CRM in one flow.

pros: Send a document for signature within minutes with no training
Embedded signing API with clear docs, SDKs and a free test mode
Executed copies land back in the originating Dropbox folder
Free plan covers occasional signing for freelancers
Qualified electronic signature support for EU business plans
cons: Little feature development since the Dropbox acquisition
No conditional fields, pre-send approvals or agreement search
API pricing scales with volume and can exceed web plan cost
verdict_line: Pick Dropbox Sign if you want the simplest signing tool or the easiest API to embed signature in your own app.

pros: Request signatures from Word, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint and Power Automate
Certifications cover eIDAS qualified signatures, FedRAMP, HIPAA and 21 CFR Part 11
Government ID, knowledge based and phone authentication for signers
Workflow designer builds conditional multi step routing without code
Best PDF rendering and field recognition in the category
cons: Bundled into several Acrobat plans, so working out what you get is hard
Interface feels dated with more clicks per send than rivals
Interesting features need business or enterprise editions
verdict_line: Pick Adobe Acrobat Sign if you live in Microsoft 365 and Acrobat and need regulated industry certifications on signing.

pros: Conditional fields, calculated fields and signing links on mid tier plans
Document groups send several files as one signing session
Collect a Stripe or Authorize.net payment at signature
Plans do not cap the number of documents sent
Strong tablet apps for in person signing
cons: No free plan, only a short trial
Less name recognition with enterprise counterparties than DocuSign
SSO, branding and detailed audit reporting need top tier packaging
starting_price: $8 per user per month billed annually
verdict_line: Pick SignNow if you want conditional fields, document groups and payments at a lower per user cost than DocuSign.

pros: Signature fields sit inside regular forms so intake and signing are one step
Approval flows and workflow builder route signed documents without extra tools
Hundreds of ready made signable templates for leases, waivers and NDAs
Free plan includes a handful of signed documents each month
cons: Signing caps are shared with form submissions and storage limits
No bulk send or advanced signer identity verification
CRM document generation is weaker than PandaDoc or DocuSign
verdict_line: Pick Jotform Sign if you already collect data in Jotform and want signatures, approvals and automations on the same submissions.
